Renovations can increase your home’s value, enhance its functionality, and create a space better suited for your needs. But while they’re in progress, these projects often cause disruptions, clutter, and other hassles that can raise stress levels.


If you’re planning to tackle a remodeling project this summer, home renovation storage can make the process a lot smoother and easier to manage.


Here’s what to know about storage for home renovations, from the benefits and options to some of our favorite tips.


## Why Home Renovation Storage and Decluttering Matter


Whether you’re remodeling the kitchen, adding a room, or converting the basement into an office, decluttering is the first step of any successful renovation project. Here are some benefits to keep in mind:


### Create More Space for Contractors


Decluttering allows for increased access to the renovation areas and more freedom of movement throughout your home. Not only will this help the contractors do their jobs more efficiently, but it can also minimize the risk of accidents for workers as well as your family.


### Get Furniture and Valuables Out of the Way


Remodeling projects can cause dust and other construction debris to collect, and also lead to scratches and dents in surrounding furniture. Moving your furniture, appliances, electronics, and other valuables to an off-site location will help keep them organized during your project.


### Reduce Stress Throughout the Project


The less cluttered your space is, the easier it is to stay organized and maintain normal routines. This means less stress day to day. If timelines stretch out, as they often do with remodeling projects, you’ll also be better prepared to adapt.


## Organization Tips for Smoother Remodeling Storage


Free image via[Pexels](https://www.pexels.com/photo/content-couple-unpacking-clothes-during-relocation-4245899/)


From keeping tasks on schedule to[packing for short-term storage](https://www.cubesmart.com/blog/your-life/how-do-you-pack-for-short-term-storage-the-complete-guide/) , organization is crucial for a streamlined renovation. Here’s a quick rundown of how to maintain an orderly space throughout this experience.


### Declutter Your Space Before Construction Begins


Every[summer cleaning list](https://www.cubesmart.com/blog/your-space/15-items-in-your-home-to-add-to-your-summer-cleaning-list/) should start with decluttering, especially when there’s a renovation on the agenda. Taking care of this before the remodel will lay the groundwork for a smoother project. Plus, the more you get rid of now, the less you’ll need to pack or keep tabs on, and the less money you’ll have to pay for home renovation storage.


### Create Zones of Separation Inside Your Home


Establishing separate zones in your home during a renovation maximizes organization and convenience, while minimizing disruptions to your routine. Partition off the construction zones from living spaces and storage areas to limit the spread of debris and dust. Off-site storage for home renovations is a great way to maximize space at home while keeping your items from potential damage.


## How to Store Stuff During a Renovation


Free image via[Pexels](https://www.pexels.com/photo/crop-man-packing-carton-box-with-scotch-tape-dispenser-4246095/)


How do you store stuff during a renovation? Once you remove non-essentials (such as furniture, decorations, seasonal items, and outdoor gear) from the construction area, you’ll need a convenient, accessible place to keep them. That’s where renovation storage solutions come in handy. Here’s how to get these items ready for temporary storage:


### Sort All Your Items Before Packing


The first step in this process is to sort all your items into distinct categories, such as the ones below. This will help you determine what exactly to do with them during the renovation.


- **Donate:** Items you no longer have a use for, but don’t want to toss out.
- **Discard:** Broken, worn out, or obsolete items that wouldn’t make sense to donate.
- **Keep on-hand:** Items you need access to, like medications, critical documents, summer clothes, household cleaners, toiletries, and cooking utensils.
- **Store temporarily:** Items you can move into[temporary storage](https://www.cubesmart.com/storage/temporary-storage/) on a monthly basis, just until the renovation is complete (think furniture, electronics, appliances, etc.)
- **Store long-term:** Items you want, but use infrequently, making them great candidates for a[long-term storage](https://www.cubesmart.com/storage/long-term-storage/) unit or[storage locker](https://www.cubesmart.com/blog/your-space/what-is-a-storage-locker-the-complete-guide/) (think winter clothes, outdoor gear, seasonal decor, etc.)


### Pack Your Items Carefully


Now it’s time to pack the items you plan on moving into home renovation storage. When packing, use these materials to keep everything secure:


- Sturdy boxes
- Plastic bins
- Heavy-duty tape
- Packing paper
- Blankets
- Furniture covers
- Bubble wrap
- Foam sheets
- Mattress bags


### Label and Inventory Each Item


Once you’ve finished packing, the last step is to label your boxes, making it easy to track your stuff in storage (e.g., “Kitchen Cutlery,” “Spare Bedroom Linens,” etc.).


Add a unique number to each box and create a thorough inventory list that will match those numbered boxes to their contents. This makes *finding* things in storage quick and easy.


**Pro tip:** Take photos of the contents of each box and tape them to the outside for easy browsing. For more tips on accessing and tracking your stored items, check out this practical guide for[how to organize a storage unit](https://www.cubesmart.com/blog/your-space/organization/how-to-organize-a-storage-unit/) .


## Benefits of Temporary Storage During Your Home Renovation


Free image via[Pexels](https://www.pexels.com/photo/happy-diverse-couple-among-carton-boxes-in-new-home-4247825/)


Self-storage is often one of the easiest home renovation storage solutions, especially for long projects or ones that involve relocating large items that can sustain costly damage, such as appliances. Let’s look at some of the best reasons to utilize temporary storage during a home renovation.


### Temporary Storage Offers a Flexible Rental Timeline


Short-term renovation storage solutions typically come with flexible monthly rental terms, making these units ideal for home renovation projects of all sizes and scopes. For instance, with a quicker remodel, you can rent a unit for the time you need without committing to a long-term contract. If construction delays arise or the project runs longer than anticipated, simply extend the rental timeline and keep your items stored until the work is complete.


### Temporary Storage Makes It Easier to Store Large Items


Unlike a handful of boxes, bulky belongings like kitchen appliances, office equipment, tables, couches, and other large furniture pieces aren’t as easy to move to other parts of your home during the construction process. This makes them ideal for keeping off-site. And, as storage units come in a variety of sizes, there should be enough room for even some of your bulkiest household items.


### Temporary Storage Has Climate-Controlled Options


Is climate-controlled storage necessary during renovations? This option is preferable for items sensitive to extreme temperatures, especially in the summer months. The most common[things that need climate-controlled storage](https://www.cubesmart.com/blog/your-space/organization/10-surprising-things-that-need-climate-controlled-storage/) include electronics and wooden furniture. Even if the remodel won’t take long, a temporary climate-controlled storage unit can help shield these items from harsh summer conditions until you’re able to move them back home.*
